states: The first Coverage disclosure remains mounted throughout reading all 16 observed provider labels at desktop and 320px; a complete scope must enter the viewport, not merely be mounted.
An ordinary same-open HTTP refresh expands the existing panel to 20 independently attributable provider observations without changing the Unknown posture or inventing restore evidence.
A single settled forward scan and a single reverse scan each bring every one of 200 workload summaries into the viewport, within 140-desktop/36-phone mounted-workload bounds.
interactions: Keyboard Enter expands the actual desktop disclosure; native phone row taps expand/collapse it in Chromium and WebKit.
Refresh backups is keyboard-activated and retains focus while the actual posture/inventory readers accept new fixtures; the existing panel stays open.

Native page scroll events advance the existing window; the scan waits at most two seconds for mounted rows to cover the actual visible table body before advancing. No event injection, threshold change, repeated favourable pass selection, mutating request or off-origin request. Browser/server both close, and no page/console error is observed.

pixel_review.limits: Pixels show selected viewport moments. Complete 16/20 provider and 200-workload reachability is separately measured by actual viewport geometry; no physical swipe, continuous-frame latency, native guest, installed or release acceptance is inferred.

limits: The original 45ms scan sampled delayed WebKit runway updates and missed rows; both original and diagnostic failures are retained. Final proof establishes bounded settled reachability, not continuous-scroll frame latency.

Source/fixture/browser proof is not independent guest thaw, every-filesystem writes, workload liveness, prior-active restoration, fresh-install recovery, protected delivery, release availability or reporter confirmation.
